title: Hansen/UMD Global Forest Change 2000–2025 (v1.13)
description: Global 30 m maps of tree canopy cover in 2000 and of annual gross forest cover loss from 2001 to 2025, derived from Landsat time-series analysis by the University of Maryland GLAD laboratory with Google, USGS and NASA. Layers include tree cover 2000 (% canopy closure of vegetation taller than 5 m), year of loss (stand-replacement disturbance), forest gain 2000–2012, a data mask, and cloud-free Landsat reference composites.
purpose: Locates and dates tree-cover loss in Algeria's northern forests (cork oak, Aleppo pine, cedar) from wildfires, clearing and dieback, providing a consistent annual series for burned-forest assessment and reforestation monitoring.

spatial_extent.description: 10° x 10° tiles spanning 180°W–180°E and 80°N–60°S. Algeria lies in tiles with top-left corners 40N_010W, 40N_000E, 30N_000E and neighbours (tiles 40N_000E, 40N_010W and 30N_000E were confirmed to exist for v1.13).

temporal_extent.description: Tree cover baseline for 2000; annual loss for 2001–2025; gain only for 2000–2012. Only the 'lossyear' and 'last' layers are updated annually, with a new version number each year.

variables.name: treecover2000
variables.description: Canopy closure in 2000 of vegetation taller than 5 m (0–100)

variables.name: lossyear
variables.description: 0 = no loss; otherwise year of gross loss minus 2000 (2001–2025)

variables.name: datamask
variables.description: 0 no data, 1 mapped land, 2 persistent water (2000–2012)

variables.name: first / last
variables.description: Landsat red, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2 composites for ~2000 and ~2025

processing: Supervised classification of Landsat time-series metrics on Google Earth Engine. Version 1.13 reprocesses 2011 onward with Landsat 8 and 9 data and a revised model; earlier years were not reprocessed. Loss is defined as a stand-replacement disturbance (forest to non-forest), and gain as the inverse of loss within 2000–2012.
validation: Accuracy assessment is reported in Hansen et al. (2013). The v1.13 page warns that the maps are a relative indicator of trends and that 'definitive area estimation should not be made using pixels counts from the forest loss layers'; sample-based estimation is required for area statistics.
limitations: Pixel counts of loss are biased area estimates; use a probability sample for official-style statistics.

Changes in sensors (Landsat 7 scan-line failure, Landsat 8/9), data volume and algorithm (v1.0 for 2000–2012 vs v1.13 for 2011–2025) make year-to-year comparisons uncertain; the provider recommends caution and temporal smoothing (e.g. 3-year averages).
'Tree cover' is any vegetation taller than 5 m, so orchards, olive groves and date-palm plantations may be included; it is not a legal forest definition.
Loss includes all stand-replacing causes (fire, clearing, harvest, dieback) without attribution of driver; gain is only available for 2000–2012.
Vegetation lower than 5 m (matorral, shrubland) is by definition not tree cover, and loss in sparse woodland depends on the canopy threshold chosen by the user.

algeria_notes: Forest and pre-forest cover is concentrated in the Tell Atlas (Kabylie, El Kala, Aurès, Ouarsenis). Loss years coincide with major fire seasons, but loss is not attributed to fire; cross-check with MODIS MCD64A1 burned area or FIRMS. Post-fire regrowth after 2012 is not captured, because the gain layer covers only 2000–2012. Saharan tiles contain essentially no tree cover.

unverified_fields: validation figures (not transcribed from Hansen et al. 2013)
verification.notes: Licence, layers, definitions, caveats and tiling were read from the v1.13 download page. The page text for 'lossyear' still says 'a value in the range 1-20, representing loss detected primarily in the year 2001-2025' — the range appears not to have been updated; codes are year minus 2000. Tile existence over Algeria was confirmed with HTTP HEAD requests (40N_000E, 40N_010W, 30N_000E lossyear files, HTTP 200). The glad.umd.edu dataset page returned HTTP 404 and was not used.
